guidance: A jar test measures settled volume, while the USDA classes are defined on particle weight, so treat the result as an estimate and repeat the test or use a laboratory particle-size analysis when the sample sits near a class boundary.
method: Soil texture is the weight share of sand, silt and clay in the fine-earth fraction (under 2 mm). The page turns three settled depths, or three laboratory percentages, into shares of 100 and then applies the twelve class definitions of the USDA Soil Survey Manual, chapter 3, figure 3-7: sand is more than 85% sand with silt plus 1.5 times the clay under 15; loamy sand is 70 to 90% sand with silt plus 1.5 times the clay 15 or more and silt plus twice the clay under 30; sandy loam is 7 to under 20% clay with more than 52% sand, or under 7% clay with under 50% silt, and silt plus twice the clay 30 or more; loam is 7 to under 27% clay, 28 to under 50% silt and 52% or less sand; silt loam is 50% or more silt with 12 to under 27% clay, or 50 to under 80% silt with under 12% clay; silt is 80% or more silt with under 12% clay; sandy clay loam is 20 to under 35% clay with under 28% silt and more than 45% sand; clay loam is 27 to under 40% clay with more than 20 to 45% sand; silty clay loam is 27 to under 40% clay with 20% or less sand; sandy clay is 35% or more clay with more than 45% sand; silty clay is 40% or more clay with 40% or more silt; and clay is 40% or more clay with 45% or less sand and under 40% silt. A percentage entry must add up to within half a point of 100 and is normalised when it does not; a depth entry is converted to millimetres only to refuse a sample under 1 mm, because the shares do not depend on the unit. Settled layers measure volume while the classes are defined on weight, and clay flocculates differently from sand, so a jar reading estimates rather than reproduces a laboratory analysis; organic matter floating on top is not part of the mineral texture and is left out. The class is named exactly, and a sample that would change class after a 1.5-point shift between two separates is flagged as near a boundary. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: USDA NRCS, Soil Survey Manual (Agriculture Handbook No. 18, 2017), chapter 3, "Definitions of Soil Texture Classes and Subclasses" and figure 3-7, the twelve texture classes and their sand, silt and clay limits
